transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess what finally made me call is I’ve been having some thoughts that scared me a bit. Like… if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, maybe that would be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, but… it bothered me enough to come in.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
Not… not exactly killing myself. It’s more like I’ve had thoughts that if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, it might be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, but it scared me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Yeah… I think so. Most mornings lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like everything’s already sort of drained before I even get dressed for work.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Probably… around six months. It’s been this low, flat sort of feeling, and after a while even my usual things, like walks or art class, stopped really helping.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I guess I have. I still get my paints out sometimes, or think about going to pottery class, but then I’m just sort of sitting there staring at everything. It doesn’t feel the way it used to. That spark is… mostly not there.
Did this low mood start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

I guess it kind of lines up with work… the trouble with the new district manager. This whole up-and-down thing with my mood and energy has been going on maybe two months, since that started getting bad.
If the problems at work were suddenly resolved, do you think this low mood would mostly lift?
I don’t know. Maybe a little, if that pressure was gone… but I’m not sure it would just fix everything.
Before these past six months, was there a stretch of at least two months when you were not feeling depressed?
No… I don’t think so. It’s been more like this flat, low stretch for about six months now. My usual things—art class, morning walks—they haven’t really helped the way they used to.
Before this current six-month period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had rough patches before, but I don’t know if I’d call them like this, or if they lasted two weeks.
When something good happens, does your mood actually lift for a while?
A little, maybe… but it doesn’t last much. Most mornings I still wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like everything’s kind of drained out before I even get going.
Have you noticed a change in your sleep?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really been tracking it. I guess nothing that stands out to me.
Have you been feeling worthless?
Yeah… sometimes. I’ll get stuck on small things at work, like if a sign wasn’t straight or someone I’m training seemed confused, and then I start thinking I’m just… not any good at being in charge.
When you’re away from work for a day or two, do you feel noticeably less depressed?
Not really. Even if I’m off for a day or two, most mornings I still wake up with that heavy, gray feeling… like the color’s drained out before I even get dressed.
Before these past six months, were you generally feeling down or low most of the time for years?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that. I’ve had rough stretches, sure, but I don’t think it was most of the time for years.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… some. Little decisions take longer than they should. Like at work, deciding which endcap to reset first, or even at home picking out a blouse—I’ll just stand there kind of foggy, second-guessing myself.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot?
I don’t know… not a lot, I don’t think. I get tense sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it as being on edge all the time.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
Not really… I mean, I haven’t noticed much of a change either way.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Maybe a little. I don’t know if people have noticed, but some days I catch myself pacing and picking at my cuticles… and then other days I feel oddly slow, even just walking back out to the sales floor.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?
Yes… somewhat. Even when I’ve been in bed all night, I still feel worn out. Little things at work, like opening the store or answering a few staff questions, take more out of me than they should.
Before this six-month period, was there ever another time when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. Nothing that clearly stands out to me like that, no.
